 Rasmus Ristolainen returns as Matvei Michkov stays in lineup amid trade rumors
 Defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen returns to the lineup for the Flyers against Edmonton on Wednesday night, while winger Matvei Michkov participated in the game-day skate.
 Posted on November 11, 2026 November 11, 2026 by Jason MacNeil 
 Heather Barry Images 
 While it seems like a secondary story compared to the reports which broke Tuesday evening , the Philadelphia Flyers will have a few changes to personnel and the forward lines as the team faces the host Edmonton Oilers on Wednesday night.
 According to Philadelphia Inquirer beat reporter Jackie Spiegel , defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen will be returning to the lineup this evening and the rest of the lineup will be as follows:
 Michael Bunting — Christian Dvorak — Owen Tippett
Tyson Foerster — Trevor Zegras — Travis Konecny
Porter Martone — Noah Cates — Matvei Michkov
Denver Barkey — Sean Couturier — Noel Acciari
 Travis Sanheim — Jamie Drysdale
Cam York — Oliver Bonk
Nick Seeler — Rasmus Ristolainen
 Dan Vladar
(Joseph Woll)
 Prior to the Anaheim game, Ristolainen had missed the previous three weeks due to injury. In four games this season, the blueliner has a goal and no helpers, while averaging 17:21 in ice time. The Flyers will see Travis Sanheim and Jamie Drysdale as the top pairing, while Cam York and Oliver Bonk will be the middle pairing against Connor McDavid and the high-octane Oilers.
 The addition of Ristolainen means that David Jiricek, who played Monday evening against Vancouver, will be out of the lineup yet again as a healthy scratch. Jiricek was paired with Simon Benoit on the ice Wednesday, but both most likely will be watching the game from the press box. 
 Cole Knuble will also be a healthy scratch for the second consecutive game, as well. The 22-year-old missed the game in Vancouver after Tocchet’s attempt to mold him into a middle-six center against the Flames the night prior. Philadelphia has only 13 forwards on the roster so it’s not like he will spend much time on the sidelines or be sent down, but Michael Bunting scoring against the Canucks is probably the reason why the veteran is still in the lineup and Knuble is out.
 Michkov skates, Bunting bumped up
 Perhaps the biggest news thus far was that Matvei Michkov was on the ice practicing with the Flyers after reports surfaced on Tuesday night inferring he wanted out of town . Michkov was on a line with Noah Cates and Porter Martone, a line that was establishing some chemistry the last few weeks before being split up briefly. 
 As small as the news was, it might have been a small baby step in the right direction regarding the club and the forward. If Flyers general manager Danny Briere opted to look at trading Michkov following the reports last night, there’s a very good chance Michkov would be not playing to simply keep him healthy for potential suitors around the league. However, by seeing him on the ice, at least for now, there seems to be some semblance of peace between Michkov, his camp, and the organization. In addition to Briere, Flyers President of Hockey Operations Keith Jones, and Team Governor Dan Hilferty, were also attending Wednesday’s game-day skate in Edmonton , a clear indication the organization is trying to get control of this possible worst-case scenario.
 Elsewhere, Michael Bunting — who scored his first of the season against Vancouver on Monday night — will be with center Christian Dvorak and Owen Tippett on a line. Bunting, who would be relegated to a bottom-six or fourth-line role on most teams, is going to have a chance to play with some top-six forwards in the hope some sort of synergy, chemistry, or lightning in a bottle emerges. Elsewhere, Tyson Foerster and Travis Konecny will be wingers with Trevor Zegras playing down the middle against the Oilers. Finally, Denver Barkey and Noel Acciari will find themselves on either side of Sean Couturier.
 Finally, Dan Vladar will get the start. Vladar’s last start was in Calgary, an overtime loss that Vladar was instrumental in getting to the extra period.
 The Flyers will look to not get completely destroyed against McDavid and his Oilers. Maybe they can take a point and while playing awful hockey games, can say they took four our of a possible six points in this Western Canada swing of their road trip.
